newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Int'l hopes to resume flights by Nov. 20.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Int'l hopes to resume flights by Nov. 20.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines hopes to return to the skies by November 20, an attorney for the bankrupt airline said Thursday.
"We hope to have a partial flight schedule in the air by November 20," said Kiwi attorney Howard Greenberg said, following a bankrupcty court hearing in Newark.
"You can assume we would want to get back in the air by Thanksgiving," said Kiwi spokesman Rob Kulat.
Kiwi suspended operations on October 15, after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 30, 1996 under a $40 million debt load.
Kiwi plans to outline its return to scheduled service at a November 4 press conference.
Greenberg said he expects the company to recall about 800 of the 1,200 employees that were laid off, but he declined to comment on when those employees might return to work.
Also at the bankruptcy hearing, U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Rosemary Gambardella approved Kiwi's $5 million debtor-in-possession financing commitment from the Wasatch Group.
The judge said she expects Kiwi's Chapter 11 bankruptcy to be resolved after a final court hearing on November 22.
